dedupe_keys.name: en 50600 and iso iec 22237 data centre facilities and infrastructure standards

description: EN 50600 is the European series of standards for data centre facilities and infrastructures, and ISO/IEC 22237 is the international series based on it. Together they set out how a data centre should be designed, built and operated for a chosen level of availability, physical security and energy efficiency, with parts on general concepts, building construction, power distribution, environmental control, telecommunications cabling, security systems and management and operational information, and a related set of key performance indicators such as power usage effectiveness (the EN 50600-4 and ISO/IEC 30134 parts). The standards define four availability classes: class 1 with single components and one distribution path, class 2 with redundant components, class 3 concurrently maintainable with multiple paths, and class 4 fault tolerant. These map roughly, but not exactly, onto the four ratings of ANSI/TIA-942 and the four tiers of the Uptime Institute, which are governed and assessed differently, and third-party bodies certify facilities against them. Coverage: generic, applied in Europe and worldwide. Format and access: standards documents sold by national standards bodies, ISO and IEC; summaries free from certifiers and trainers. Caveats: paid documents; certification is voluntary and sites rarely publish their class. Simulation uses: parameters for redundancy and failure paths in data-centre reliability models, and a common vocabulary for resilience classes in scenario studies. Related records: the Uptime Institute outage analysis links outages to design and operation.
